newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker, hit new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker, hit new contract lows.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures fell to fresh life-of-contract lows almost across the board, while the spot-Januray contract settled below support.
Analysts said today's losses were technical in nature. But with adequate supplies forecast for both the U.S. and Brazil, the fundamental indicators also point to lower prices.
"Overall, the bearish tone has been triggered by the funds and prospects for higher supplies that has weighed on prices," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
"Now is a continuation of the bearish trend."
January closed down 1.55 cent a lb at 94.90, having ranged from 96.80 to 94.60, a fresh life-of-contract low. The deferred months finished down 1.80 to 1.20.
Georgakis said light support could be found around 94.00 cents and then around 92.00 cents in January. She said today's close below previous support of 95.00 does not bode well for the market.
FCOJ futures will not trade Thursday and Friday due to the Thanksgiving holiday.
